mcq.question: Why is `badge != nullptr && badge->active` safe even when `badge` is null?

options.A: `badge->active` returns false for a null pointer
options.B: The compiler reorders the operands to check `active` last
options.C: Dereferencing a null pointer inside a condition is defined behaviour
options.D: `&&` short-circuits: when the left operand is false the right operand is never evaluated

mcq.explanation: The built-in `&&` guarantees left-to-right evaluation and skips the right operand when the result is already known. Dereferencing a null pointer would be undefined behaviour.

mcq.question: Which expression is equivalent to `!(has_badge && has_clearance)`?
mcq.explanation: De Morgan's law: negating an AND turns it into an OR of the negations. The door is refused if at least one requirement is missing.

bonus.question: Short-circuit evaluation means side effects in the right operand may not happen. Should conditions ever contain side effects? Give an example where it causes a bug.
Write a failing test proving that `can_enter` never reads the badge's clearance during a lockdown (use an `EvaluationTrace`-style spy), then restructure the expression so it passes.
